draft.title: Protein structure
card: Amino acids join by peptide bonds to form a chain called a polypeptide. The order of amino acids in the chain is the primary structure.
Parts of the chain fold into coils (alpha helices) and pleats (beta pleated sheets), held by hydrogen bonds. This is the secondary structure.
The whole chain then folds into a 3D shape, the tertiary structure. Bonds and attractions between the side groups of amino acids hold this shape.
Some proteins have two or more polypeptides joined together. This is the quaternary structure. All of an organism's proteins together make its proteome.
draft.remember: Sequence, then coils and pleats, then 3D fold, then joined chains. Shape decides function.

a.q: What is the primary structure of a protein?
opts: The sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide
The coils and pleats in part of a polypeptide
The 3D shape of one whole polypeptide
Two or more polypeptides joined together
a.why: Primary structure is only the order of amino acids in the chain. Coils and pleats are secondary structure, and the 3D fold of the whole chain is tertiary.
a.clue: Think about the first level, before any folding.

b.q: A protein is made of four separate polypeptides that join to work as one unit. Which level of structure does this joining describe?
opts: Quaternary structure
Tertiary structure
Secondary structure
Primary structure
b.why: Quaternary structure is the joining of two or more polypeptides. Tertiary structure is tempting, but it describes the fold of a single polypeptide chain.
b.clue: Count how many chains are involved.

a.best: The sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide
